subject: ambient observation has atomic privacy admission, end-to-end provenance, and pressure-aware cadence
defects_closed: ambient privacy admission expected an app and title from get_window_title even though that provider returned only the title, leaving app-only private surfaces such as password managers unidentifiable on the production path
frontmost app and title had no atomic host observation contract, so separate reads could describe different windows across a focus change
ambient observations discarded host-automation receipt identity, adapter, and duration at both context and capture boundaries
the ambient loop polled at a fixed cadence without consulting foreground inference, proof, memory, compute, or failure pressure
a malformed receipt duration or unavailable background policy could terminate the continuous perception organ
the shell-gateway routing unit test depended on persisted live approval state instead of isolating the gateway behavior it names

implementation.privacy_admission: one read-only AppleScript receipt atomically returns the frontmost application and its current window title before any screen capture is attempted
implementation.provenance: context and capture adapter, receipt ID, and bounded duration flow through ScreenContext, TickResult, Observation detail, and privacy-safe state telemetry
implementation.failure_behavior: malformed telemetry normalizes to zero and a policy lookup failure records a degradation then sleeps at bounded configured backoff rather than killing the loop
implementation.test_isolation: the post-action shell gateway test supplies its execution authorization fixture; execution-authority semantics remain owned by their dedicated contracts

verification.live_rebuilt_app: deferred while the resident-32B proof campaign owns the model budget and Aura.app is intentionally stopped

claim_boundary.reason: bounded contracts prove the production code paths; rebuilt native-bubble and changing-page behavior still require a live app after the model campaign releases the host
